title: Distributive vs. Integrative Mindset
description: Distributive = dividing a fixed pie (price, salary). Integrative = expanding the pie by trading things each side values differently.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Distributive = dividing a fixed pie (price, salary). Integrative = expanding the pie by trading things each side values differently.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: Distributive: A used-car buyer and seller only talk about price.
Integrative: A job negotiation where the candidate trades a later start date for a higher salary, or extra vacation days for a slightly lower bonus.

sections.title: Tactics to Identify Integrative Potential
content: Ask: 'What's most important to you besides price?'
Listen for statements like 'We really need speed on this' or 'Cash flow timing matters a lot for us.'
Offer multiple equivalent packages (e.g., higher salary with less vacation vs. lower salary with more vacation) to see which is preferred.

sections.title: Common Mistake
sections.content: Treating every negotiation as purely distributive. Most real-world deals have multiple issues where preferences differ.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
sections.content: Always list at least three issues to negotiate, not just one. If you're only talking about money, you're likely stuck in a fixed-pie battle.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Value is created when you give the other side something they value more than it costs you.
